digest.component_or_area: S3 remote store recovery / multi-bundle healing
propositions: When two bundle objects exist for the same ref on S3, git-remote-s3's cmd_push rejects the push before writing and fetch cannot resolve the ambiguous ref, stalling all push retries and making the store unclonable.

Upstream's Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocking input() prompts) and discards non-chosen heads, causing data loss of ticket events unique to those heads in an append-only event log.

The heal must acquire the helper's per-ref lock, re-enumerate bundles, fetch all divergent heads, merge them losslessly via iterated 2-parent git merges, write the merged bundle before deleting originals, and ensure every crash point leaves ≥1 bundle carrying full merged history.

The merge algorithm must follow sync's existing _union_merge semantics: 2-parent merge (not octopus), explicit --allow-unrelated-histories for unrelated heads, abort on genuine content conflict (never discard), and .bridge_state merge=ours for derived files.
The doctor must run under rebar's write_lock to prevent races with local committers, with the helper's S3 lock as the outer lock and write_lock as inner, creating a fixed cycle-free order.

The heal must be invoked from push_tickets_branch on multi-bundle signature detection with a healed_once guard to prevent retry thrash, using lazy git-remote-s3 import behind require_s3_helper() and transitive boto3 to avoid adding direct S3 SDK dependency to core rebar.
